key: That be far from Thee to do after this manner, to slay the righteous with the wicked, that so the righteous should be as the wicked; that be far from Thee; shall not the judge of all the earth do justly?’
s: As the LORD prepares to destroy Sodom and Gomorrah for their sin, Abraham pleads for the cities; the Midrash, Genesis Rabbah 49:9, reads his question as an argument that a world cannot endure strict justice unless God yields a little.

evidence.words: אִם עוֹלָם אַתָּה מְבַקֵּשׁ אֵין דִּין, וְאִם דִּין אַתָּה מְבַקֵּשׁ לֵית עוֹלָם, אַתְּ תָּפֵיס חַבְלָא בִּתְרֵין רָאשִׁין, בָּעֵי עָלְמָא וּבָעֵי דִינָא, אִם לֵית אַתְּ מְוַתֵּר צִבְחַר, לֵית עָלְמָא יָכֵיל קָאֵים
evidence.gloss: Rabbi Levi, on “Shall not the judge of all the earth do justly” (Abraham arguing): If You seek a world, there is no strict justice; and if You seek strict justice, there is no world. You are holding the rope at both ends: You want the world and You want strict justice. If You do not yield a little, the world cannot stand.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Genesis 18:25, at [17,25]). Opened the Genesis Rabbah packet for 18:25: in 49:9 Rabbi Levi takes Abraham’s question “shall not the judge of all the earth do justly” as the argument that a world cannot stand on strict justice unless God yields a little (the same saying recurs in 39:6); the reading is his, at the place named, and adds nothing. Plain sense faithful: the LORD speaks of the outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah and the cities are destroyed in chapter 19 of the same day; Abraham pleads. The proposer’s evidence string had its niqqud marks in a different code-point order from the packet, so the evidence here is recopied character for character from the packet. Entry unchanged; entry-check ok.
